Hi Alice / Connor — attaching the requested artifacts and a short summary of options. Attachments: SOC2_Snapshot_Mar2027.pdf, redwood_private_deploy_options.pdf, medicover_network_diagram_v1.png

Executive summary:
- SOC 2: Redwood completed a SOC 2 Type II for the period ending 2026-12. The attached snapshot contains the auditor opinion, tested control list and evidence buckets. We have a control mapping template filled for the most common procurement questions; happy to map to your template if you send it.

- GDPR / DPA: We provide a DPA and support EU data residency options via regional private clusters. For Private deployments in your VPC we can restrict egress and ensure data never leaves the assigned region. We will call out specifics in the DPA draft.

- Deployment topology options (high-level):
  1) Hosted Private (recommended first step) — Redwood-managed control plane with customer VPC peering (private endpoints). Pros: quick onboarding, managed updates, logs forwarded to customer SIEM. Cons: control plane metadata still in Redwood control plane (can be mitigated with contractual controls).
  2) Customer-managed VPC (preferred for strict network controls) — deployment nodes run in customer VPC, customer manages NAT/egress, and we optionally integrate with customer KMS. Pros: full network isolation, customer controls egress. Cons: more operational onboarding and runbook requirements.
  3) Air-gapped on-prem (highest control) — installs into your air-gapped environment; requires offline package delivery and a snapshot upgrade process. Pros: maximal isolation and meets most regulatory needs. Cons: feature latency for updates, reduced ability to perform remote troubleshooting, longer lead times and additional support contract.

Security controls & operational notes:
- Encryption: data at rest encrypted using AES-256, and we support customer-managed KMS for encryption keys.
- Logging & audit: we can forward audit logs to your SIEM and provide attested log retention policies.
- Access controls: RBAC for token scopes + recommended 2-person approval flows for key changes.
- HIPAA: Redwood has experience enabling HIPAA controls for customers; enabling HIPAA workloads requires Business Associate Agreement (BAA) + some onboarding steps (audit evidence and controlled environments).

Next steps (proposed):
1) Connor/Medicover: confirm which topology to prioritize (1, 2, or 3).
2) Marissa: we will produce the DPA draft and control mapping against Medicover template if provided (ETA: 2 business days).
3) Neha: will share the three diagrams and a short runbook excerpt for the air-gapped option (ETA: 2 business days).

Links: DPA draft workspace (https://drive.redwood.com/file/d/diagram-id/view) and HubSpot record: https://app.redwood.com/hubspot/contacts/medicover-4721
